I farm a small 4.1 mu wheat-maize rotation field, so I will keep the whole plot in the same system this year. Because I have 30 years of experience and I can irrigate from a well, I will stay with the kind of management that is steady and practical rather than risky. For wheat, I will use an improved seed, put in moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few key times, and protect the crop with a couple of pesticide sprays because wheat yield on my land depends on keeping the stand even and avoiding losses. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same 4.1 mu because hybrid maize gives me more stable production. I will use a bit more nitrogen for maize than for wheat, irrigate when the crop most needs water, and do basic pest control without overdoing it. I will use simple tillage methods that match a small household farm and aim for reliable yields instead of chasing the very highest output.
